answer: Withdrawing stake costs a 4% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the prism fee is applied at the raven exit, the canyon audit totals the burn and the ledger makes public exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 34 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
